title: Dataset Distillation via Knowledge Distillation: Towards Efficient Self-Supervised Pre-training of Deep Networks

contributions.purpose: Enable dataset distillation (DD) for self-supervised (SSL) pre-training, an open problem, so a tiny synthetic set can pre-train high-quality encoders when labeled data is scarce.
contributions.mechanism: MKDT (Matching Knowledge Distillation Trajectories): (1) train a large teacher encoder with SSL (e.g. BarlowTwins), (2) train small student encoders to match the teacher's representations via a knowledge-distillation MSE objective to get lower-variance expert trajectories, (3) generate synthetic data by trajectory-matching those student trajectories. KD objective has much lower variance than the SSL loss, making trajectory matching feasible.
contributions.evaluation: Distill CIFAR10, CIFAR100, TinyImageNet down to 2% and 5% of original size; across various downstream tasks with limited labels MKDT outperforms all baselines (incl. KRR-ST, SAS, random real) by up to 13% accuracy; transfers from ConvNet-distilled sets to ResNet-18; works with BarlowTwins and SimCLR.
contributions.source_quote: In this work, we propose the first effective DD method for SSL pre-training. ... we train a small student model to match the representations of a larger teacher model trained with SSL. Then, we generate a small synthetic dataset by matching the training trajectories of the student models.

contributions.purpose: Explain why prior supervised DD methods (gradient/distribution/trajectory matching) fail when transferred to SSL.
contributions.mechanism: Theoretical and empirical analysis of trajectory variance: measure variance of SSL vs SL trajectories over lengths, distillation loss curves for MTT-SSL vs MTT-SL, and pixel-change of synthetic images; also test 4x batch size to reduce variance.
contributions.evaluation: SSL trajectories have larger and faster-growing variance than SL; MTT-SSL distillation loss decreases slowly and synthetic images barely move from initialization; 4x batch size only slightly reduces variance and is insufficient; gradient/distribution matching need labels (representation collapse otherwise).
contributions.source_quote: First, we show, theoretically and empirically, that naïve application of supervised DD methods to SSL fails, due to the high variance of the SSL gradient.

self_declared_provenance.quote: MTT is another dataset distillation method that is agnostic to the labels, and hence can be potentially applied to SSL. Nevertheless, application of MTT to SSL has not been explored before. In our work, we show that that naïve application of MTT to SSL yields poor performance. Then, we propose a method that leverages knowledge distillation to enable effective dataset distillation for SSL.

While KRR-ST also uses a MSE loss to representations instead of directly performing SSL, they claim to do so to mitigate the bias of bi-level optimization in meta-model based matching for SSL. In MKDT, we instead, use the knowledge distillation loss of MSE to representations of a larger teacher model to reduce the high variance of SSL gradients.
Here, we rely on the knowledge distillation objective for SSL models, introduced in Yu et al. (2019)

notes: Builds directly on MTT (Cazenavette et al. 2022) trajectory matching and the SSL-KD MSE objective (Yu et al. 2019). Reports a negative result about prior work: KRR-ST distilled sets do NOT outperform SSL pre-training on random real examples ('SSL pre-training on these distilled sets does not provide any advantage over SSL pre-training on random real examples'). Also negative baseline finding: subsets most beneficial for supervised learning are least beneficial for self-supervised contrastive learning. Main claimed gain is up to 13% over prior work.
